thread:
anya: Quick sync — proposing a dedicated capability-handshake endpoint and a client-side contract for model features. Goal: replace brittle per-model docs + scattered flags with a single /capabilities handshake that SDKs can call and cache. Outline below, want launch criteria and prioritization.

devon: sgtm. can you clarify token_limit semantics early? customers keep asking whether limits include system prompts and streaming buffers.

anya: Proposal (rough):
```
GET /v1/models/:id/capabilities
Response 200 {
  "capabilities": ["chat","embeddings","rerank","functions","streaming","structured_output"],
  "tools": [{"name":"http_call","version":"1.0","schema_url":"https://.../tools/http_call.v1.json"}],
  "max_tokens_per_request": 65536,        // hard cap per client call
  "max_tokens_including_system": 61440,   // conservative usable tokens after system role
  "streaming": true,
  "structured_output_versions": ["1.0","0.9"],
  "cache_ttl_seconds": 300,
  "capability_hash": "sha256:..."
}
```
Note: response shown as example only. We should explicitly document that max_tokens_* are enforced at runtime and may differ per route (chat vs embeddings).

mike: Love the hash. Add a `schema_url` for the whole capabilities response so clients can validate. Also: prefer `capability_profile` objects instead of flat list so we can annotate per-route limits (applies_to: ["chat","completion"]).

oliver: Agree. Also recommend returning `cache_control` headers and `X-Redwood-Capabilities: <hash>` so SDKs can do conditional fetches. TTL should be short-ish for rapid rollouts but long enough to avoid thundering.

sophie: Launch checklist idea (high level):
- api spec + example responses documented
- SDK: handshake function + cache helper
- Contract tests (unit + integration) against Dedicated/private envs
- Perf tests (latency, token accounting, streaming correctness)
- Migration guide for customers + sample client code
- Rollout plan with canary and automatic fallback mapping
(we should pick owners for each)

devon: FYI customer ask: Acme AI needs streaming + functions + 65k token effective budget. They want an SLA for steady-state throughput. If we can encode fallback mapping in the capabilities response (e.g., `fallback_model: "gptx-medium-quant"`), customers can programmatically degrade.

anya: Prioritization suggestion:
1) capability endpoint + cache header + schema_url (MVP)
2) SDK handshake + sample migration (critical for PLG)
3) per-route limits & tool manifests (next sprint)
4) structured_output schema hosting + examples
5) perf & dedicated capacity validation

Launch criteria (proposed):
- API contract tests pass (including negative cases: missing fields, truncated tool list)
- SDK handshake exists in node/python/ts and is used in at least 2 internal demo apps
- No token-accounting regressions on Dedicated (within 3% of baseline)
- Customer migration guide published + one pilot customer signed up for early access

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy of feature/capability-handshake branch to staging at 23:00 UTC. CI pipeline: 12/12 checks passing.

oliver: Edge cases to document: model variants with different streaming behavior, per-route overrides (applies_to), and private deployments where control-plane introspection may be restricted (we may need a flag `control_plane_only: true`).

mike: Question: for private deployments, will the handshake endpoint live on customer control plane or on every runtime? If control plane only, we need a secure, low-latency cache strategy for on-prem. Also think about auth scope: token introspection + rate limit IDs.

anya: Good catch. Proposal: default: control-plane introspection, runtime can optionally expose a local endpoint for low latency with an audit-only sync back to the control plane. Doc this as a permitted config.

devon: on it :thumbsup: I can stub the API and tests. I'll include examples for streaming clients showing how to read the capability hash and fall back.

anya: I'll draft the PR with the detailed spec and a checklist of contract tests by EOD. Owners: devon (api + tests), oliver (cache headers + schema design), mike (contract tests + private deployment notes), sophie (docs + migration).

sophie: I'll write a short migration guide template, include sample curl + node code snippets and a bullets list for customer communications.

anya: Thanks all. If no blockers I'll upload the first draft in this thread later today. :rocket:
